explanation: `extChartAt_model_space_eq_id (x : E) : extChartAt 𝓘(𝕜, E) x = PartialEquiv.refl E` (line 866, same file/section) is the function-level form of the same fact about exactly the same object as the judged theorem `{x y : E} : extChartAt 𝓘(𝕜, E) x y = y`. The two differ only in presentation (function equality vs. its pointwise application); applying `DFunLike.congr_fun` at `y` gives `extChartAt 𝓘(𝕜, E) x y = ⇑(PartialEquiv.refl E) y`, and the right-hand side is definitionally `y` since `PartialEquiv.refl_coe` (Logic/Equiv/PartialEquiv.lean:533) is `rfl` and `id` is reducible, so the derivation closes by `rfl` (or by `simpa`). No argument is instantiated to anything specific. The judged proof is `rfl`, and `ext_chart_model_space_apply` is not tagged `mfld_simps`, so `extChartAt_model_space_eq_id` (proved by `simp only [mfld_simps]`) is independent of it. A second, weaker route exists via the general `extChartAt_self_apply {x y : H} : extChartAt I x y = I y` with `I := 𝓘(𝕜, E)` plus `modelWithCornersSelf_coe`, but the equality-of-functions statement above is the exact analogue. I also checked for `_apply`/`_eq_id` variants of this statement elsewhere in Mathlib; `ext_chart_model_space_apply` itself is the only pointwise form.
